Developing Web Applications with KoldFusion

Welcome to CFML

A KoldFusion page is called a template. It is an ordinary HTML file with a .cfm extension and a few extra tags mixed in. When a browser asks for the page, the web server hands it to KoldFusion, which runs the CFML tags and sends plain HTML back. The browser never sees your CFML, only its results, so the pages work in any browser, from Navigator 4.7 to Lynx.

CFML tags look like HTML tags whose names start with CF: CFSET, CFOUTPUT, CFIF, CFQUERY and so on. You write them in the same editor you use for HTML, save the file anywhere below the web root (wwwroot) and browse to it. There is nothing to compile.

Your first template

The CFOUTPUT tag tells KoldFusion to look for expressions in the text it encloses. An expression is anything between a pair of pound signs, such as #Now()#. KoldFusion replaces it with its value; everything else passes through unchanged.

ch1_hello.cfmRun this example · View source
<!--- ch1_hello.cfm: a first KoldFusion template.
      Comments with three dashes are removed by the server
      and never reach the browser. --->
<HTML>
<HEAD><TITLE>Hello from KoldFusion</TITLE></HEAD>
<BODY BGCOLOR="#FFFFFF">
<FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica" SIZE="2">

<H2>Hello, world!</H2>

<CFOUTPUT>
<P>Today is #DateFormat(Now(), "dddd, mmmm d, yyyy")#
and the server clock says #TimeFormat(Now(), "h:mm tt")#.</P>

<P>Only #DateDiff("d", Now(), CreateDate(2000, 1, 1))# days left
until the year 2000. (If that number is negative, congratulations:
you made it.)</P>

<!-- An HTML comment with two dashes is sent to the browser. -->
<P>Inside CFOUTPUT a literal pound sign is written twice: ##1 on the charts.</P>
</CFOUTPUT>

<P>Outside CFOUTPUT, #Now()# is just text.</P>
</FONT>
</BODY>
</HTML>

Notice the last line: without CFOUTPUT around it, the expression is not evaluated. And because # has a special meaning inside CFOUTPUT, you must double it when you want a real pound sign, for example in a color attribute such as BGCOLOR="##FFFFCC".

Comments

CFML comments use three dashes: <!--- ... --->. KoldFusion strips them out before the page is sent, so they are the right place for notes about your code. Ordinary HTML comments (two dashes) are passed through to the browser, where anyone can read them with View Source.

Variables

The CFSET tag creates a variable or changes its value. Variable names start with a letter and may contain letters, digits and underscores. Names are not case sensitive: FirstName, firstname and FIRSTNAME are the same variable. Values are not typed in advance; a variable holds whatever you put in it, whether a string, a number, a date or a Boolean (YES/NO) value.

ch1_variables.cfmRun this example · View source
<!--- ch1_variables.cfm: setting and showing variables --->
<CFSET Product = "56K V.90 Fax/Modem">
<CFSET Price = 129.99>
<CFSET Quantity = 3>
<CFSET Total = Price * Quantity>
<CFSET OrderDate = Now()>
<CFSET IsRush = Quantity GT 2>

<CFOUTPUT>
<TABLE BORDER="1" CELLPADDING="4" CELLSPACING="0">
<TR BGCOLOR="##CCCCFF"><TH>Item</TH><TH>Qty</TH><TH>Total</TH><TH>Rush?</TH></TR>
<TR>
  <TD>#Product#</TD>
  <TD ALIGN="RIGHT">#Quantity#</TD>
  <TD ALIGN="RIGHT">#DollarFormat(Total)#</TD>
  <TD>#YesNoFormat(IsRush)#</TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>
<P>Ordered on #DateFormat(OrderDate, "mm/dd/yyyy")#. Raw values:
Total = #Total#, IsRush = #IsRush#.</P>
</CFOUTPUT>

Formatting functions such as DollarFormat, DateFormat and YesNoFormat turn raw values into something fit for people. Notice that the Boolean result of Quantity GT 2 prints as YES; numbers print without trailing zeros.

Note  Use pound signs only where KoldFusion would otherwise see plain text: inside CFOUTPUT, or inside a quoted attribute value. In <CFSET Total = Price * Quantity> no pound signs are needed, and adding them (#Price#) only makes the code harder to read.
